question_en: What species is the insect in the image? Please provide the scientific name.
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 2-2-D03

## Step 01 · Extract visible morphology only from current photos A and B

**Action:** Combine long antennae, green leaf-like wings, and hind leg morphology for retrieval, for example `leaf katydid broad flattened tibial spines` or `green katydid robust hind legs triangular spines`.

**Evidence Observation:** The current input consists only of photos A and B. The insect has very long antennae, leaf-like green wing surfaces, and robust hind legs; particularly striking are the broad, flat, triangular spines on the hind tibiae. Photo A shows a frontal posture, while Photo B shows the body and raised hind legs from an oblique side angle. The full wing length and the complete dorsal spine row on the hind femur are insufficient in these views for independent confirmation; the photos lack a scale bar, so actual body length cannot be measured.

**Result of this step:** The search narrows down to leaf katydids / katydids with distinctive hind leg spines, rather than directly identifying the species based solely on green color or leaf-mimicking appearance.

## Step 02 · Use diagnostic criteria and original images from taxonomic papers to filter candidates together

**Action:** Check the original taxonomic paper by Ghirotto et al. published in 2025 in the "European Journal of Taxonomy"; read the diagnosis on page 282 and view Figure 17 on page 301; the Figure 17 record on Zenodo can serve as the entry point for the original images.

https://doi.org/10.5852/ejt.2025.1007.3013

https://zenodo.org/records/16918203

https://zenodo.org/api/records/16918203/files/figure.png/content

**Evidence Observation:** The genus diagnosis in the paper specifies robust legs and broad, flat hind tibial spines, which explains the most distinctive combination in the input. The top row A and B of Figure 17 correspond to the current input: Photo A shares the same frontal standing posture, antenna orientation, oblique leaf angle, and reflection position; Photo B shares the same leg-raising posture, foot placement, and light-colored spots on the supporting leaf. Although the remaining C–F images in the original figure can be seen in the paper, they are not part of the problem statement and cannot be used to supplement morphological features not shown in the input.

**Result of this step:** Established correspondence with the original photos; this provides greater identification power than general similarity based on "also having broad wings and spiny legs." The next step is to read the figure caption to determine the species.

## Step 03 · Read the holotype figure caption without misrepresenting the entire diagnosis as visual observation

**Action:** Verify the complete caption for Figure 17 and the species entry on page 284 to link the photos, scientific name, and specimen identity.

https://doi.org/10.5852/ejt.2025.1007.3013

**Evidence Observation:** Figure 17 explicitly states that the photographed subject is a live male holotype of `Metallacantha aculeata`, housed at DZUP, and notes that the photos are not to scale. A and B are different postures of this same holotype. Page 282 also describes diagnostic features such as the dorsal spine row on the femur, but the current photos A and B are insufficient to independently verify these details; female structures, male genitalia, hind wings, and calling songs are not evidence visible in the problem images. The species name is explicitly confirmed by the same figure and the holotype caption, without relying on fabricated invisible features.

**Result of this step:** Achieved direct identification evidence at the species level; the candidate is Metallacantha aculeata.

## Step 04 · Use sourced neighbors to check limitations of similar appearances

**Action:** Compare with the neighbor discussion on page 305 of the paper, and view the Paracycloptera gallery at UNLP, the Tanusiella travassosi specimen at OSF, and the adult Arachnacris corporalis photos at HMNS.

https://biodar.unlp.edu.ar/tettigoniidae/en/info/20248.html

https://biodar.unlp.edu.ar/tettigoniidae/images/346.jpg

https://orthoptera.speciesfile.org/otus/850411/overview

https://blog.hmns.org/2022/09/where-do-baby-bugs-come-from/

**Evidence Observation:** Reference photos of Paracycloptera also show green leaf-like wings and light-colored lateral bands, indicating these features are not unique; however, the hind legs in that image are thinner and lack the prominent broad triangular tibial spines seen in the target images. There are unresolved issues regarding the specific species in that gallery, so the comparison stops at the genus level. The preserved female specimen of Tanusiella shows short wings, fine dense wing venation, and thinner legs; the brown color of the preserved specimen is not used as a hard exclusion criterion. The live adult image of Arachnacris from HMNS shows thinner, longer legs and finer spines, differing from the target's robust hind legs and broad flat spines. Comparing these photos explains why common leaf katydid names are insufficient for species identification, but this does not equate to an exhaustive list of all katydids; the matched original holotype image remains the decisive evidence.

**Result of this step:** Neighbor comparison is consistent with the attribution of the original image; there is no requirement to see complete short wings or the complete femoral spine row in A and B before providing an answer.

## Step 05 · Verify scientific name spelling and provide binomial nomenclature

**Action:** Check the naming and holotype records in the Orthoptera Species File entries to verify the genus name, specific epithet, and cited paper.

https://orthoptera.speciesfile.org/otus/1138108

**Evidence Observation:** Professional indices list `Metallacantha aculeata` along with the 2025 naming author information, pointing to the same original paper and the DZUP male holotype. This is a verification against naming indices, not a second independent discovery or experiment; the Zenodo images and the paper also share the same source. The question only requires the scientific name; it is unnecessary to append all naming authors, and even more so to fabricate unverified Chinese common names.

**Result of this step:** The scientific name and the identity of the photographed specimen are confirmed; stop retrieval.

**Formal Answer:**

Metallacantha aculeata
